rationale: A wins because it stays a little more disciplined about what the facts can carry and gives the founder cleaner go/no-go gates. Its strongest line, "Whoop puts FDA-cleared AFib detection behind its most expensive tier," is a real launch-day conflict with obvious proof needs; B's "A blood-pressure feature that needs a blood-pressure cuff to work" is sharper copy, but it leans on an invented prevailing belief that "wearables are replacing clinical instruments." Both sets are strong, but A is less tempted to make the category story bigger than the evidence.
gaps_in_A: "Whoop finally ships the ECG its rivals already have" is useful but slightly underpowered as a headline; without naming or timing competitors, it risks reading as generic catch-up unless the proof work lands.

"The blood-pressure estimate is Whoop's possible differentiator, but only if the user can show rivals lack one" is properly cautious, but it leaves the founder with a weak category claim until competitor evidence is gathered.
"Story type: defensive-comment" for the tier-gating angle is an odd label for what is really a consumer-business/pricing accountability story.
A could have made the cuff-calibration contradiction its own angle; it captures it inside other angles but misses B's cleaner consumer-scrutiny shape.
gaps_in_B: "The prevailing belief is that wearables are replacing clinical instruments" is not in the update. That is the kind of grand category premise that sounds smart until a reporter asks who actually said it.

"the differentiating claim is blood pressure — a feature nobody has cleared" overreaches. The update says Whoop's blood-pressure estimate is not diagnostic and that competitors have ECG; it does not prove nobody has cleared cuffless blood pressure.
"Whoop's entire model is subscription rather than hardware margin" is plausible brand knowledge, but it is not supplied in the facts. In a blind grounding test, that is a leak.

"Next step: newsjack-detector" is the wrong default for a product launch with four already viable launch angles. Run fit-check after filling proof gaps; don't go hunting for a fabricated stronger peg.
